briefings.title: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

people.name: Benedict Evans
people.role: Independent Analyst & Former Partner, Andreessen Horowitz

briefings.tldr: AI is a monumental platform shift equivalent to—but only equivalent to—the internet or mobile revolutions.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
AI is a monumental platform shift equivalent to—but only equivalent to—the internet or mobile revolutions. Because we are currently in its chaotic "1997" era, long-term value will not accrue to commoditized foundational models but to the specialized application layer, custom enterprise integrations, and distribution moats.

---

## The "1997" Timeline of AI and the Illusion of AGI

* **The 1997 Analogy:** Tech analyst Benedict Evans argues that we are currently in the "1997" equivalent of the AI lifecycle. 
    * **Immaturity of Tech:** Most tools do not fully work yet, enterprise sales cycles are long, and predicting the dominant players today is as futile as crowning Excite or Yahoo the winners of the early web.
    * **Adoption Gaps:** While tech insiders use LLMs hourly, mainstream adoption remains shallow; data shows only 15–20% of teens use AI daily, while 60% do not use it at all.
* **Redefining AI and AGI:** Evans notes that "AI" is a moving target that refers only to technology that has not been normalized yet.
    * **The Larry Tesler Quote:** "AI is whatever machines can't do yet." Once a system successfully performs a task, people dismiss it as "just software" (e.g., databases, OCR, and sentiment analysis).
    * **Goalpost Shifting:** The definition of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) is being actively watered down by model labs to mean "economically valuable work," a benchmark that mainframes in the 1970s already partially achieved.

## Deconstructing the "Job Apocalypse" and the Task vs. Job Fallacy

* **The Jevons Paradox of Labor:** Throughout history, automation has not led to permanent mass unemployment.
    * **Price Elasticity:** Making a task cheaper (e.g., accounting via spreadsheets, writing code via IDEs) dramatically increases total demand rather than reducing headcount. Despite centuries of automation, employment and GDP continue to rise.
    * **Unknown Roles:** Historical shifts show that you can easily see the job that will be automated away (e.g., typesetters, elevator operators), but you cannot see the new jobs because they do not exist yet.
* **The "Boring Manual Labor" of Coding:** Software engineering is currently the most transformed industry because LLMs revealed that massive portions of coding are actually repetitive, manual tasks.
    * **Shift in Focus:** Just as 90% of modern iOS code is pre-written by Apple drivers, AI allows developers to build complex applications faster, shifting their primary role from writing code lines to software architecture and product-market strategy.
* **The Error of Expert Systems Metrics:** Evans dismisses government and consulting datasets (like O*NET) that try to predict exactly what percentage of a profession (e.g., "17% of a lawyer's work") can be automated.
    * **Complex Realities:** Human professions are organic webs of politics, customer relationships, and physical realities that cannot be cleanly broken down into logical steps.

## The Commoditization of Foundational Models and Value Capture

* **No Network Effects for Models:** Foundational model labs (such as OpenAI and Anthropic) currently lack strong, winner-take-all network effects.
    * **Low-Margin Utilities:** Without structural differentiation, these labs risk ending up like global telecom carriers or cloud hosting providers—selling a highly sophisticated, capital-intensive commodity at marginal cost with zero pricing power.
* **The Rise of "Forward-Deployed" Engineering:** Foundational model labs are aggressively buying consultancies and hiring professional services teams.
    * **Enterprise Bottleneck:** Modern enterprises do not have idle, highly skilled employees sitting around to completely redesign internal workflows. Integrating AI requires heavy manual consulting lifting from firms like Bain, McKinsey, or Accenture.
* **The Power of Distribution:** As software becomes easier and cheaper to build, noise in the market escalates, making distribution the ultimate moat.
    * **Incumbent Advantages:** Companies with existing distribution networks (like Google with Android/Workspace or Meta across social feeds) can easily deploy "adequate" commoditized AI to millions of users, winning through convenience and default settings.

## Navigating the Anti-AI Backlash and Cultural Anxiety

* **Exaggerated Resource Panic:** Evans notes that many public concerns about AI are a "fuzzy mess of truth and fiction."
    * **The Water cooling Myth:** While data center expansion is a real localized planning and electricity challenge, its overall environmental impact is often overstated. A Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory study estimated US data center water consumption at just 0.017% of total US water use.
* **Real and Decentralized Harms:** The real societal threat of AI is not an existential machine takeover (the "Doomer" narrative), but localized, decentralized malice.
    * **The Photoshop Parallel:** Photoshop has always allowed people to falsify images, but AI lowers the technical barrier, allowing anyone to generate complex deepfakes in minutes, causing immediate societal harm.
* **The Only Viable Professional Strategy:** Evans warns against adopting an attitude of moral superiority or avoidance regarding AI.
    * **Involvement is Mandatory:** The only way to survive the transition is to dive deep into the technology to understand exactly what it can do and how it can augment your unique skillset.

---

> "My most controversial opinion is that I think that AI is as big a deal as the internet or mobile and only as big a deal as the internet or mobile." 
> — Benedict Evans

> "Every time we have a new technology, it automates away a bunch of jobs, and then that automation unlocks a bunch of new jobs. And you don't know the new job because it doesn't exist yet."
> — Benedict Evans

> "AI is whatever machines can't do yet. Because once machines can do it, people say, 'Well, that's just software.'"
> — Benedict Evans (quoting Larry Tesler)

> "You talk to these doomers on Twitter... and they would act like every big company is going to buy ChatGPT tomorrow, and then in two weeks' time, they'll fire all their staff. These people are morons."
> — Benedict Evans

briefings.title: 'GET THIS MACHINE GOING': Jamie Dimon calls for a new American industrial buildout
briefings.tldr: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon is calling for a massive $1.5 trillion domestic and allied industrial buildout over the next decade to secure supply chains, while warning that underlying inflation risks make him "cautiously pessimistic" about the long-term economy.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon is calling for a massive $1.5 trillion domestic and allied industrial buildout over the next decade to secure supply chains, while warning that underlying inflation risks make him "cautiously pessimistic" about the long-term economy. Dimon also urged policymakers to enforce banking rules on crypto platforms, establish a "Manhattan Project" for AI cybersecurity, and reform local policies to solve the housing crisis.

---

## Economic Outlook, Monetary Policy, and Banking returns
* **The Macro Picture:** The U.S. economy is currently stable with 2% growth, 4.3% unemployment, and strong corporate profits fueled by significant deficits and stimulus (including $300 billion in legislative spending and $300 billion in AI investments).
    * **Inflation and Consumer Strain:** Dimon is more concerned than most, describing himself as "cautiously pessimistic." Rising inflation and higher gas prices are forcing lower-income consumers to deplete their savings and increase borrowing.
    * **Market "Melt-Ups":** Despite two ongoing global wars, the NASDAQ rose 28% in late spring. Dimon warns that market run-ups often last longer than expected before reversing due to shifts in sentiment, interest rates, or consumer demand.
* **Overearning and Excess Capital:** JPMorgan is currently generating a 20% return on tangible common equity, surpassing its 17% target. Dimon calls this "overearning" due to temporarily high margins and trading volumes, warning that competitive and credit cycles will eventually normalize. 
    * **Share Buybacks:** JPM is continuing buybacks but prefers to deploy its estimated $40 billion in excess capital toward organic business growth or potential acquisitions in wealth management or fintech.
* **Federal Reserve Leadership:** Dimon highly praises new Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh and supports his goal to shrink the Fed’s balance sheet. 
    * **Regulatory Relief:** Dimon argues that simplifying complex liquidity rules (like LCR and SLR) would allow banks to safely deploy a portion of JPM's $1.2 trillion in cash and Treasuries back into active market lending.

## The $1.5 Trillion Security & Resiliency Initiative
* **Rebuilding the Industrial Base:** Recognizing critical dependencies on adversaries for active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), rare earth elements, military drones, and shipbuilding, Dimon has launched a $1.5 trillion, 10-year "Security and Resiliency Initiative."
    * **Direct Investments:** JPM has already invested $2 billion directly into middle-market defense and infrastructure companies.
    * **Allied Expansion:** The initiative is expanding beyond the U.S. to allied nations, including the UK, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Australia, Japan, South Korea, and Canada.
* **WWII-Scale Ambition:** Citing the book *Freedom's Forge*, Dimon highlighted how the U.S. rapidly converted commercial factories to build 144 aircraft carriers in four years during WWII. He calls for a similar policy-driven urgency to keep defense factories warm during peacetime.
* **The China Strategy:** Following a recent trip to China and Taiwan, Dimon confirmed that JPM banks approximately 2,000 multinational corporations in China. He supports the U.S. government’s strategy of "full engagement" while strictly enforcing sanctions and protecting national security interests.

## Technological Disruption: AI Risks, Fintech, and Crypto
* **AI Cybersecurity and "Mythos":** While AI will drive massive productivity and medical breakthroughs, Dimon warns that powerful models like Anthropic's "Mythos" can rapidly expose zero-day software vulnerabilities.
    * **Mini Manhattan Project:** Because hackers can now exploit vulnerabilities in hours rather than weeks, Dimon recommends a government-led "mini Manhattan Project" to secure critical infrastructure (water, electricity, telecom) against ransomware.
    * **Jobs Impact:** AI will replace some jobs while creating others. Dimon advises against panicking, calling on local community colleges and unions to quickly retrain workers for open trade jobs.
* **The Fight Over Crypto and the Clarity Act:** Dimon is strongly opposed to the current draft of the Clarity Act, which would allow stablecoin issuers to pay interest on deposits.
    * **Regulatory Fairness:** Dimon argues that if platforms like Coinbase act like banks, they must be subject to the same strict regulations, including anti-money laundering (AML), Bank Secrecy Act (BSA), Know Your Customer (KYC), and FDIC requirements.
    * **Fintech Competitors:** JPM views firms like Revolut, Stripe, Chime, Dave, SoFi, PayPal, Brex, and Citadel as far more formidable and direct competitors than stablecoin projects.

## Housing, Domestic Policy, and the American Dream
* **The American Dream Initiative:** Launched in March, this initiative focuses on boosting homeownership, small business growth, and financial literacy for the bottom 20% to 30% of the U.S. income scale. JPM aims to expand its small business reach from 7 million to 10 million clients.
* **Zoning and Mortgage Reform:** Dimon attributes the lack of affordable housing to restrictive local zoning laws. 
    * **Regulatory Cost Reduction:** He asserts that streamlining redundant federal rules around mortgage securitization, origination, and servicing could reduce mortgage costs by 50 basis points for lower-income buyers.
* **Competing Cities:** In a polite but direct meeting with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Dimon emphasized that cities must actively compete to keep businesses by managing individual/corporate tax rates and maintaining basic quality of life (policing, sanitation, and hospital systems).

---

## Notable Quotes

> "America is still the beacon of light on the hill, still the arsenal of democracy, the bastion of freedom... the strongest military in the world, underpinned by the strongest economy in the world. If those two things disappear, so will dollar dominance one day."
— **Jamie Dimon**

> "If he [Coinbase] takes deposits like a bank, he should have bank rules... We have like 84 regulators all over us. We're just saying it should be fair and equal, period."
— **Jamie Dimon**

> "We went from building a liberty ship in one year to two days. And, so it's just—we just got to get this machine going and hopefully this will get it done fast enough."
— **Jamie Dimon**

> "I always refer to [these issues] as tectonic plates moving around, that may cause issues that we don't fully understand today... My probabilities of a worse outcome are higher than other people's, and it's mostly around inflation."
— **Jamie Dimon**
